title: A 24-million-character tag prefix used by 64,000 nodes that alternate between two suffixes, in a document that is edited
notes: The document declares `%TAG !e! tag:x,2000:` followed by 24 million `a` (a run of URI characters, section 6.8.2, production 93 via [88]). A block sequence of 64,000 items follows, alternating `!e!x` and `!e!y`; the tag of each is the prefix followed by the suffix (section 6.9.1), a string of 24 million characters. A reader that keeps the last resolved tag in a one-entry cache builds a new 24-million-character string at every item, and one that stores each node's resolved tag holds 64,000 of them. The sibling case with one suffix is passed by the one-entry cache; alternating suffixes defeat it. The case appends one item (`add` at the end of the sequence) and nothing else, so the answer is the input followed by `- z`, or a limit error; a patch, because a value or events result would have to state the full tag of every node, which no stored expectation can hold. An unrecognized-tag error is not accepted: the document is well-formed and an edit of its presentation needs no native value. The time limit is 30 seconds and is a hang guard, not a measure of cost. The prefix is as long as it is so that the guard still has force: a reader that builds the tag of every node, even if it throws each string away at once, copies 24 million characters 64,000 times, 1.5 trillion bytes, and a model reader that does nothing but allocate, copy and free needed 117 seconds at 13 GB/s; a reader that keeps the strings goes over the memory bound long before that. Readers that work through the prefix once needed between 1.5 and 2.5 seconds. A prefix of a million characters, as this case used before, left that model reader at about two and a half seconds, far inside the guard. The memory is the whole adapter process, and the input is about 24 MB. The limits are the robustness requirement of the kit, not a rule of the specification. The input and the expected result are generated from the recipe in case.json (docs/case-format.md).

provenance.reference: A tag cache of one entry that missed on every node of a document whose tags alternate between two suffixes.
